Title: The changing rationalities of Australian federal and national inclusive education policies | The Australian Educational Researcher | Springer Nature Link
In this article, we examine the development of inclusive education policies by Australian federal governments over the last 30 years, with a specific focus on policies relating to disabilities. It is pertinent to focus on the development of inclusive education policies at the federal level because while successive Australian federal governments have played leading roles in driving national reform to the education of students with disability, few studies have been completed that provide historical and conceptual accounts of these developments. This broader trend is reflected in disability education policies, where successive federal governments have driven national reforms relating to the education of students with disabilities, especially following the legislation of the *Disability Discrimination Act* (DDA) in 1992, which mandates that individuals with disabilities have the right to access and participate in mainstream schools. While successive Australian federal governments have played a prominent role driving national reform of the education of students with disabilities, few studies have been completed that provide a historical and conceptual analysis of the development of inclusive education policies at the national scale. Three distinct phases of policy development are identified, which we suggest are characterised by three dominant rationalities: (1) *standardisation*, which privileges standards, consistency, coordination and alignment as policy solutions; (2) *the neo-social*, which frames social goods such as inclusion as primarily important for their role in fostering greater economic productivity; and (3) *personalisation*, which suggests that the quality of a public service (such as education) can be enhanced through tailoring it to the needs and preferences of the individual citizen/consumer. The shift towards emphasising the economic benefits of creating a more accessible, inclusive, and equitable education observable in the Standards foreshadowed how in the subsequent decade a neo-social rationality that melted together social and economic goals became the dominant framing in national and federal disability policy. Another central shift, is that in contrast to the dominant rationality of standardisation during the first phase, whereby creating a more coordinated and consistent national approach to policy was framed as key to creating a more inclusive school system, the rationality of personalisation rests on a view that school systems can chiefly be made more inclusive through teachers tailoring education to students’ individual needs and aspirations.

results.title: Solved: Discuss the social and human dimensions of development.
results.content: Solved: Discuss the social and human dimensions of development. Discuss the social and human dimensions of development. The social and human dimensions of development revolve around improving individual well-being and expanding freedoms. Social development emphasizes enhancing citizens' capabilities through better access to education, healthcare, and housing, thereby addressing social factors like poverty and inequality. In contrast, human development often measures progress using the Human Development Index (HDI), which incorporates indicators of health (life expectancy), education (years of schooling), and standard of living (income). Understanding the interconnectedness of economic growth, equity, and public policies is crucial for achieving sustainable development. Initiatives promoting inclusive community projects can serve as practical examples of integrating these dimensions for holistic societal improvement. **1.** To address the question of discussing the social and human dimensions of development, we first need to understand the definitions and distinctions between "social development" and "human development." Social development focuses on improving individual well-being and ensuring that all citizens can contribute to society, while human development emphasizes expanding people's freedoms and improving their quality of life. **2.** Next, we should explore the Human Development Index (HDI) as it measures key dimensions of human development: health, education, and standard of living. The HDI combines four indicators: life expectancy at birth (health), mean years of schooling for adults (education), expected years of schooling for children (education), and gross national income per capita (standard of living). **3.** Additionally, it is important to consider the significance of social factors such as poverty, access to education, healthcare, and housing. These social determinants play a critical role in shaping individual lives and societal progress. Improving these factors is essential to achieving broader social and human development goals. **4.** We should also reflect on the interconnectedness of economic growth and human development. As economic opportunities expand, so must the access to education and healthcare, leading to better overall human development outcomes. **5.** Finally, we need to conclude with examples of initiatives or case studies that highlight successful integration of social and human development strategies. 83%(5 rated)What are the Seven (7) Traits of Being Human? 100%(2 rated)List the seven typical steps in developing a policy. 100%(2 rated)Solve 2x+3<7.

results.title: Education & Social Policy Studies | MVNU
results.content: # Education & Social Policy Studies. The Bachelor of Arts in Education and Social Policy Studies is designed for students interested in the field of education but not necessarily in teacher licensure. Students in the major will develop knowledge and skills related to learning theory, sociological theory, child and adolescent development, social and education policy, social services, and advocacy. Course work draws from the fields of education, psychology, sociology, social work, and business to prepare graduates to think holistically about support systems and structures that serve children, adolescents, and marginalized populations and to work in a variety of education and social services roles. Students in this major will select one of the following concentrations to further focus their studies on a topic, population, or career field: **Community Leadership Studies, Curriculum and Instruction Studies, Early Education and Child Studies, or Human Services and Social Policy Studies.**. The interdisciplinary program will prepare you to work in education and social services fields in a variety of roles. You'll take course work in education, social work, psychology, sociology, and business in order to help you better understand educational and social services structures. results.content: School ofEducation and Social Policy. # Human Development and Social Policy. * Human Development and Social Policy. ## Our Academic Programs. The School of Education and Social Policy offers the study of human development and public policy at the undergraduate and doctoral level. ## PhD in Human Development and Social Policy. A fully funded, 5-year doctoral program grounded in the study of relations between public policy and human development. ## Undergraduate Concentration in Human Development and Social Policy. In the undergraduate program, students investigate how families, schools, communities and the workplace influence human development. ## Why Human Development and Social Policy. ## In Our Students Words. Students of the highly regarded Human Development and Social Policy (HDSP) program at Northwestern's School of Education and Social Policy gain methodological and content expertise through a distinctive interdisciplinary approach. ## Why Human Development and Social Policy Matters. HDSP students will develop the ability to communicate findings in written and oral fashion to diverse audiences. These audiences might include: other researchers, policymakers, practitioners, and/or the public. For some students, it may be important to be able to situate their work in and communicate findings to international audiences. HDSP students will be able to leverage their interdisciplinary training to communicate their findings to researchers across disciplinary lines. They will be able to communicate through a range of modalities (including social media) the relevance and importance of findings in non-technical language to policymakers, practitioners, and the public. ## Connections PhD Preparation Workshop. A day-long PhD preparation and community-building workshop for members of minoritized and underrepresented communities who are considering applying to doctoral programs. ## HDSP PhD Alumni. Students apply their expertise and training to various sectors and industries after graduating from HDSP.
